title: CHAIR & 7 DRAWER DESK WITH HUO...
reason: Large 1930s-style seven-drawer kneehole desk with chair, pale Huon pine-looking drawer linings and a claimed Tasmanian maker; attribution unverified from photos but a decent regional piece.
findings: Photos 1 and 3: seven-drawer kneehole pedestal desk (three drawers in each pedestal plus one central frieze drawer) in figured reddish-brown mahogany-type veneer (species not confirmed) with plain pyramid-shaped timber knobs, a low raised back gallery, plinth base and a loose glass top. A small brass key is in the top right drawer lock. A separate dark-timber chair with a vertical slat back and cream upholstered seat is pictured with it. Photo 2 (drawer open): pale yellow drawer lining consistent with Huon pine (not confirmed from the photo), dovetailed front corners, and a flat brass lock-keeper strip on the drawer edge. No maker's label, stamp or brand is visible anywhere, so the Hewett & Inglis attribution in the title is unverified; a quick web search found no record of the firm.
condition: Veneer looks sound with ordinary age wear and no obvious loss; polish slightly dull; glass top loose; one lower knob looks slightly rotated; runners and underside not seen.
rescore_note: Neat 1930s style seven-drawer kneehole desk in figured mahogany-type veneer with pale, probably Huon pine, drawer linings plus a slat-back chair, sound condition; no maker's mark (Hewett & Inglis unverified) and brown furniture is a soft market, so mid band.
